spots.name: Rideau Canal
spots.summary: The Rideau Canal is a 202-kilometre long canal that links the Ottawa River at Ottawa with the Cataraqui River and Lake Ontario at Kingston, Ontario, Canada.

spots.name: Parliament Hill
spots.summary: Parliament Hill is an area of Crown land on the southern bank of the Ottawa River that houses the Parliament of Canada in downtown Ottawa, Ontario. It accommodates a suite of Gothic revival buildings whose architectural elements were chosen to evoke the history of parliamentary democracy.

names.ja: パーラメント・ヒル (カナダ)

spots.name: Maman
spots.summary: Maman (1999) is a bronze, stainless steel, and marble sculpture in several locations by the artist Louise Bourgeois. The sculpture, which depicts a spider, is among the world's largest, measuring over 30 ft high and over 33 ft wide (9.27 × 8.91 × 10.24 metres). It includes a sac containing 32 marble eggs.

spots.name: Centre Block
spots.summary: The Centre Block is the main building of the Canadian Parliament buildings on Parliament Hill, in Ottawa, Ontario, containing the House of Commons and Senate chambers, as well as the offices of a number of members of parliament, senators, and senior administration for both legislative houses.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Arctic.gnome assumed (based on copyright cl

spots.name: Rideau Hall
spots.summary: Rideau Hall is the official residence of the governor general of Canada, the representative of the monarch of Canada.

spots.name: National Gallery of Canada
spots.summary: The National Gallery of Canada, located in the capital city of Ottawa, Ontario, is Canada's national art museum. The museum's building takes up 46,621 square metres (501,820 sq ft), with 12,400 square metres (133,000 sq ft) of space used for exhibiting art.

spots.name: Canadian Museum of History
spots.summary: The Canadian Museum of History is a national museum on anthropology, Canadian history, cultural studies, and ethnology in Gatineau, Quebec, Canada. The purpose of the museum is to promote the heritage of Canada, as well as support related research.

names.de: Kanadas Nationalmuseum für Geschichte und Gesellschaft

spots.name: Peace Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Peace Tower is a focal bell and clock tower sitting on the central axis of the Centre Block of the Canadian parliament buildings in Ottawa, Ontario.

spots.name: National War Memorial
spots.summary: The National War Memorial, titled The Response, is a tall, granite memorial arch with accreted bronze sculptures in Ottawa, Ontario, designed by Vernon March and first dedicated by King George VI in 1939.

names.fr: Monument commémoratif de guerre du Canada
names.zh: 渥太華國家戰役紀念館

spots.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica is a Roman Catholic minor basilica in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada located on 385 Sussex Drive in the Lower Town neighbourhood. It was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1990.

spots.name: Château Laurier
spots.summary: The Fairmont Château Laurier is a 660,000-square-foot (61,000 m2) hotel with 429 guest rooms in the downtown core of Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. Located near the intersection of Rideau Street and Sussex Drive, it is designed in a French Gothic Revival Châteauesque style to complement the adjacent Parliament buildings.

names.zh: 劳里埃城堡费尔蒙酒店

spots.name: Canadian War Museum
spots.summary: The Canadian War Museum (CWM) is a national museum on the country's military history in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. The museum serves as both an educational facility on Canadian military history and a place of remembrance.

spots.name: 24 Sussex Drive
spots.summary: 24 Sussex Drive is the official residence of the prime minister of Canada, in the New Edinburgh neighbourhood of Ottawa, Ontario. Built between 1866 and 1868 by Joseph Merrill Currier, it has been the official home of the prime minister since 1951.

spots.name: Office of the Prime Minister and Privy Council
spots.summary: The Office of the Prime Minister and Privy Council building, formerly known as the Langevin Block, is an office building facing Parliament Hill in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Office of the Prime Minister and Privy Council

names.fr: Bureau du Premier ministre et du Conseil privé
names.ja: 連邦政府ランジュバン棟

spots.name: Canadian Museum of Nature
spots.summary: The Canadian Museum of Nature is a national natural history museum based in Canada's National Capital Region. The museum's exhibitions and public programs are housed in the Victoria Memorial Museum Building, a 18,910-square-metre structure (203,500 sq ft) in Ottawa, Ontario.

spots.name: Ottawa station
spots.summary: Ottawa station, or Ottawa Train Station, is the main inter-city train station in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. It is located 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) east of downtown Ottawa, adjacent to Tremblay O-Train station in the neighbourhood of Eastway Gardens.

spots.name: Library and Archives Canada

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Library and Archives Canada is the federal institution tasked with acquiring, preserving, and providing accessibility to the documentary heritage of Canada. The national archive and library is the 16th largest library in the world.

names.ja: カナダ国立図書館・文書館
names.zh: 加拿大国家图书档案馆

spots.name: Canada Aviation and Space Museum

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed

spots.summary: The Canada Aviation and Space Museum is Canada's national aviation history museum. The museum is located in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, at Ottawa/Rockcliffe Airport.

names.fr: Musée de l'aviation et de l'espace du Canada
names.it: Museo dell'Aviazione e dello Spazio del Canada
names.ja: カナダ航空宇宙博物館

spots.name: Library of Parliament

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Library of Parliament is the main information repository and research resource for the Parliament of Canada. The main branch of the library sits at the rear of the Centre Block on Parliament Hill in Ottawa, Ontario. The library survived the 1916 fire that destroyed Centre Block.

spots.name: West Block
spots.summary: The West Block is one of the three buildings on Parliament Hill, in Ottawa, Ontario. Since 28 January 2019, it has housed the interim House of Commons Chamber, installed to accommodate the House while the Centre Block is closed.

spots.name: Valiants Memorial
spots.summary: The Valiants Memorial is a military monument located in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. It commemorates fourteen key figures from the military history of Canada.

spots.name: Senate of Canada Building
spots.summary: The Senate of Canada Building is a government building and former railway station that serves as the temporary seat of the Senate of Canada. Located at 2 Rideau Street in downtown Ottawa, it was known as Ottawa Union Station and served as the city's central railway station from 1912 until 1966.

spots.name: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
spots.summary: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is a tomb situated before the National War Memorial in Confederation Square, Ottawa, Ontario.

spots.name: Bank Street
spots.summary: Bank Street is the major commercial north–south street in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

spots.name: Confederation Square
spots.summary: Confederation Square is an urban square in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, and is considered the second most important ceremonial centre in Canada's capital city, after Parliament Hill.

spots.name: Memorial to the Victims of Communism
spots.summary: The Memorial to the Victims of Communism – Canada, a Land of Refuge is a monument in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. It was officially unveiled on December 12, 2024.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Memorial to the Victims of Communism (Canada)

names.fr: Le monument aux victimes du communisme – Le Canada, une terre d'accueil
names.es: Monumento a las Víctimas del Comunismo - Canadá, una tierra de refugio
names.it: Memoriale per le vittime del comunismo (Canada)

spots.name: Ottawa Jail Hostel
spots.summary: The Ottawa Jail Hostel is a hostel operated by Saintlo Hostels and located at 75 Nicholas Street in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. The hostel was originally the Carleton County Gaol (jail), more commonly known as the Nicholas Street Gaol or Ottawa Jail.

spots.name: East Block
spots.summary: The East Block is one of the three buildings on Canada's Parliament Hill, in Ottawa, Ontario, containing offices for parliamentarians, as well as some preserved pre-Confederation spaces.

spots.name: Lansdowne Park
spots.summary: Lansdowne Park is a 40-acre (16 ha) urban park, historic sports, exhibition and entertainment facility in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, owned by the City of Ottawa. It is located on Bank Street adjacent to the Rideau Canal in The Glebe neighbourhood of central Ottawa.

spots.name: Canada Science and Technology Museum
spots.summary: The Canada Science and Technology Museum is a national museum of science and technology in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. The museum has a mandate to preserve and promote the country's scientific and technological heritage. The museum is housed in a 13,458 square metres (144,860 sq ft) building.

names.de: Kanadisches Museum für Wissenschaft und Technologie
names.fr: Musée des sciences et de la technologie du Canada

spots.name: Confederation Park
spots.summary: Confederation Park (French: Parc de la Confédération) is a public park and National Historic Site of Canada, located in the downtown core of Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

spots.name: Lisgar Collegiate Institute

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Lisgar Collegiate Institute is an Ottawa-Carleton District School Board secondary school in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. The school is located in downtown Ottawa by the Rideau Canal.

spots.name: Sparks Street
spots.summary: Sparks Street is a pedestrian mall in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. It was a main street in Ottawa that was converted into an outdoor pedestrian street in 1967, making it the earliest such street or mall in Canada.

spots.name: Canada's Golgotha
spots.summary: Canada's Golgotha is a 32-inch-high (810 mm) bronze sculpture by the British sculptor Francis Derwent Wood, produced in 1918. It illustrates the story of the Crucified Soldier from the First World War and depicts a Canadian soldier crucified on a barn door and surrounded by jeering Germans.

spots.name: Major's Hill Park
spots.summary: Major's Hill Park is a park in downtown Ottawa, Ontario. The park stands above the Rideau Canal at the point where it enters the Ottawa River.

spots.name: Cartier Square Drill Hall
spots.summary: The Drill Hall at Cartier Square is a dedicated military training facility in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. It has been a local landmark since its construction in 1879. The drill hall is 70 metres (230 ft) long and has two 43-metre-tall (141 ft) mansard towers.

names.fr: Manège militaire de la place Cartier

spots.name: Bank of Canada Museum
spots.summary: The Bank of Canada Museum, formerly known as the Currency Museum.

names.fr: Musée de la Banque du Canada

spots.name: Victoria Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Victoria Tower was the prominent main bell tower of the original Centre Block parliament building in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. The 55-metre-high (180 ft) tower was the centre piece of Parliament Hill that was constructed from 1859 to 1866 by Thomas Fuller.

spots.name: Portrait Gallery of Canada

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Portrait Gallery of Canada is a federally-registered not-for-profit corporation that currently has no collection or physical presence.

photo.author: The original uploader was SimonP at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Plaza Bridge
spots.summary: The Plaza Bridge in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, is an automotive and pedestrian bridge that crosses the Rideau Canal just south of the Ottawa locks. It joins Wellington Street and Elgin Street in the Downtown core to the west with Rideau Street to the east.

photo.author: You may select the license of your choice.

spots.name: Confederation Building
spots.summary: The Confederation Building is an office building in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. Located just west of the Parliament Buildings at Bank Street and Wellington Street, it is generally considered part of Parliament Hill.

spots.name: Kìwekì Point
spots.summary: Kìwekì Point, formerly Nepean Point, is a hill overlooking the Ottawa River in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. It is located between the National Gallery of Canada and Alexandra Bridge. The site is managed by the National Capital Commission (NCC).

photo.author: You may select the license of your choice.

spots.name: Ottawa Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Ottawa Art Gallery (OAG) (French: Galerie d’art d’Ottawa (GAO)) is a municipal gallery in Ottawa, Ontario that opened in 1988 at Arts Court.

spots.name: Canadian Museum of Contemporary Photography

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Canadian Museum of Contemporary Photography (CMCP) was a gallery of Canadian contemporary art and documentary photography. Founded in 1985 and affiliated to the National Gallery of Canada (NGC), it was housed at the National Gallery of Canada, located at 380 Sussex Drive, Ottawa.

names.fr: Musée canadien de la photographie contemporaine

spots.name: Queen's Gates
spots.summary: The Queen's Gates is the formal entrance to Parliament Hill, the location of the Canadian parliament buildings, in Ottawa, Ontario.

spots.name: War of 1812 Monument
spots.summary: The War of 1812 Monument, officially titled Triumph Through Diversity, is a bronze and stone memorial, located at Parliament Hill in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, Canada's capital.

spots.name: St. Andrew's Presbyterian Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Andrew's Presbyterian Church is the oldest Presbyterian church in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

spots.name: Peacekeeping Monument
spots.summary: Reconciliation: The Peacekeeping Monument is a monument in Ottawa, the capital of Canada, commemorating Canada's role in international peacekeeping and the soldiers who have participated and are currently participating, both living and dead.

names.fr: Monument au maintien de la paix
names.es: Monumento al Mantenimiento de la Paz

spots.name: Sir John A. Macdonald Building
spots.summary: The Sir John A. Macdonald Building is a building in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. Now owned by the federal government of Canada, the building was formerly a bank. It is located at 144 Wellington Street, at the corner of O'Connor Street, with a third frontage on Sparks Street, just in front of West Block of Parliament.

spots.name: Central Post Office
spots.summary: The Central Post Office is a historic building in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. The building was completed in 1939, replacing a Second Empire style office built in 1876. This original office was located in what is today Confederation Square, and was demolished in order to construct the grand public space.

spots.name: Aberdeen Pavilion
spots.summary: The Aberdeen Pavilion is an exhibition hall in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. Overlooking the Rideau Canal, it is located in Lansdowne Park, Ottawa's historic fairgrounds. For many years, the building was known as the "Cattle Castle", due to its use for the Central Canada Exhibition's agricultural exhibits and shows.

spots.name: Rideau Falls
spots.summary: The Rideau Falls are two waterfalls located in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, where the Rideau River empties into the Ottawa River.

photo.author: The original uploader was SimonP at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Thunderhead
spots.summary: The 2SLGBTQI+ National Monument, known as Thunderhead, is a public monument in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, dedicated to the history of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer and two-spirit communities in Canada.

spots.name: Canadian Children's Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Canadian Children's Museum (CCM) is a children's museum and exhibition operated by the Canadian Museum of History in Gatineau, Quebec, Canada. The CCM attracts about half a million visitors each year.

spots.name: Christ Church Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of Christ is the Anglican cathedral in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. The church is located at 414 Sparks Street in the northwest section of the city's downtown at the western end of Sparks Street on top of a promontory looking down to the Ottawa River.

spots.name: Wellington Building
spots.summary: The Wellington Building is a Beaux-Arts architecture office building in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. It was built between 1925 and 1927 as Canadian headquarters of the Metropolitan Life Insurance Company. The original structure was designed by D.

spots.name: Statue of Oscar Peterson
spots.summary: A statue of the Canadian jazz pianist Oscar Peterson is located at the corner of Elgin and Albert streets in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, outside Canada's National Arts Centre.

spots.name: Wellington Street
spots.summary: Wellington Street is a major street in Ottawa, Canada. It is notable for being the main street of the Parliamentary Precinct of the Parliament of Canada. It is one of the first two streets laid out in Bytown in 1826.

spots.name: Bytown Museum
spots.summary: The Bytown Museum is a museum in Ottawa located in the Colonel By Valley at the Ottawa Locks of the Rideau Canal on the Ottawa River, just below Parliament Hill.

spots.name: Confederation Boulevard
spots.summary: Confederation Boulevard is a "ceremonial and discovery route" in Canada's National Capital Region, running through Parliament Hill and encompassing downtown areas in Ottawa and Gatineau. Some of Canada's most important institutions and landmarks lie along its route.

spots.name: Supreme Court of Canada
spots.summary: Canada's highest court and the best example in Ottawa of Art Deco architecture. Its marble Grand Entrance Hall is particularly impressive. The visit includes a tour in the Federal Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court of Canada hearing room. The visits last about 30 minutes and are provided by law students hired at the Court. The Court is a 5-minute walk from Parliament. Tours are offered in Frenc

spots.name: BeaverTails

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Try the tasty BeaverTail, a fried-dough pastry associated with Ottawa, although a number of places claim to have created it. It's available in sweet and savoury versions, topped with cinnamon, sugar, icing sugar, etc. In the winter, many places will offer it on the canal. During the summer, the only places downtown to offer it are in the Byward Market on George St., and a small counter in a corner

spots.name: Coconut Lagoon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Coconut Lagoon serves Kerala cuisine, subtly different from other South Indian styles (although people kept asking for Butter Chicken so it's on the menu as well). The restaurant's executive chef and owner Joe Thottungal took the silver medal at the Canadian Culinary Championships in 2017, and the gold medal at the Gold Medal Plates Culinary Competition 2016. There are vegan-friendly dishes on the

spots.name: Di Rienzo

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: This little deli tucked away in Little Italy, a secret known to many locals, is famous for the best and freshest deli sandwiches in the city for $5 (taxes included). During the week the lineup can stretch outside the packed little store, but they are arguably the fastest sandwich makers anywhere so don't worry about a long wait. There is also another newer location run by the family at Meadowlands

spots.name: Elgin Street Diner

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A popular 24-hour diner. One of its specialties is the ESD (Elgin Street Diner) Poutine (though true Quebecers should probably abstain). Generally, poutine is French fries, served with cheese curds and gravy on top; they have several versions including the addition of caramelized onions and bacon, Montreal smoked meat, Philly steak, a four cheese blend or Chili. The substitution of mashed potatoes

spots.name: Zak's Diner

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The best milk-shakes are found at Zak's, a 24-hour diner in the Byward Market. They're really good, made with ice-cream, and for the $6.99 they cost you get a large glass full plus the shaker with what didn't fit in the glass. Other dishes are quite good, with a "more calories for your money" attitude (as illustrated by the massive amount of milkshake served), which is nicely honest about fast foo

spots.name: The Standard Luxury Tavern

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: A restaurant during the day, pumping club/lounge at night. The Standard is popular Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights with a different style of music each night. Friday is excellent old-school and modern hip-hop/R&B while Saturday is a little of everything. Excellent beer tap selection and daily drink specials.

spots.name: Pub Italia

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Sun

spots.summary: An Irish/Italian pub with hundreds of bottled beers listed in its "Beer Bible", especially Belgian. Decent pizza and pastas, but other places in Little Italy have better; you're going here for the beer, not the food. Intimate faux Medieval/Gothic décor; a bit strange, but the patio is very nice.

spots.name: La Bottega Nicastro

hours.note: Closed Fri

spots.summary: A fantastic little Italian specialty market, Nicastro's is a contender for the city's best $5 sandwiches, featuring amazing bread (esp. the focaccia) usually baked on the premises. The sit-down lunch kitchen is also well worth a visit.

spots.name: Rangoon

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: A one-of-a-kind family-run Burmese restaurant with cheap lunch specials where you can get an appetizer, main course and a drink for about $10! Try the fish noodle soup (mohingha), chicken curry or eggplant curry. A real hidden gem.

spots.name: Taqueria La Bonita
spots.summary: If you're looking for Mexican cuisine (not Tex-Mex or Cal-Mex) in Ottawa, they're worth the drive out of downtown. La Bonita is a small restaurant - while you don't need to make reservations, they're recommended during busy hours.

spots.name: Heart & Crown
spots.summary: Ottawa's largest pub complex, forming a maze of busy bars and restaurants. Including the eponymous Irish Village (loud, lots of live music) and The Heart and Crown. The fish and chips has a generous serving of fish.

spots.name: Pure Kitchen Ottawa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hip restaurant serving vegetarian and vegan food. Wraps, burgers, rice bowls, salads. Bar offers juice, beer, wine. Reservations only for parties of 6 or more. Second location in Centretown at 340 Elgin Street.

spots.name: Warehouse

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Warehouse, in the heart of Byward Market, has a sidewalk patio and a roof patio. Inexpensive meals are available. Busy every day of the week, especially after 8PM when it is mostly a bar which may have a DJ.

spots.name: Gitanes

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: French-inspired restaurant that uses local ingredients. Great wines and creative cocktails. Gitanes also has sister restaurant across the street, Gitanes Burger, with amazing burgers.

spots.name: Signatures

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: At Le Cordon Bleu Culinary Institute is a French restaurant with a five-diamond rating from CAA/AAA that is considered among the very best in the city.

spots.name: Quinn's Ale House
spots.summary: A small but cozy sports bar and pub located next to the Mayfair Theatre. Expect good pub fare, a nice ambiance and good selection of beers.

spots.name: The Rainbow Bistro

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Sun

spots.summary: Multi-story bar with live music throughout the week. Dedicated regulars mingle with local and well-known names in the jazz and blues scene.

spots.name: The Lookout Bar

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: They have a very popular "bois night" on Thursday that attracts lots of people. Drag shows on Friday and Saturday nights.

spots.name: Chez Lucien
spots.summary: Pleasant bistro and bar, serving pub fare including excellent burgers and fries. A good selection of microbrew beers.

spots.name: Dominion Tavern
spots.summary: Simple beers and some pool: picture your friend's basement apartment, even serving 40s of beer (a 40-ounce glass).
